Employment of population individuals in the labour market lives in contracts; the population's exogenous `employer` column and `employed` feature do not see it (CORE-POP migration, facts.py KNOWN_DUPLICATES pop.employer).
Employer demand for labour comes only from incumbents' support queues (rivals staffing rule); industry, science and education employers do not recruit from the population yet.
Mutual-aid associations insure job loss only; their thresholds (FR-WORK-3) are uncalibrated.

Display campaigns: attention is the reference value 1 per displayed period (work.display_attention); the in-world holdout therefore checks the mechanism, not attention; the incremental conversion ratio is not applied.
Passes are 30-day term licences of services; goods and content listings by population sellers are not modelled.

gov proposals in worlds with inst are inst decisions: 4.0 society minds (actors.negotiation) read the gov proposals table and therefore no longer vote on them there (no in-world caller of gov.propose exists in civilisations).

Earlier limitations of F+G (wave 2) that remain: source-of-funds tracing replays the ledger; platform review filters look one hop back; work.value and rivals rules uncalibrated; labour task quality formula (labor.task_quality) unchanged; subjective usefulness (6.3) not implemented.
integration_notes: CORE-POP (social/creators.py, SP-6.2): route creator memberships through subs: create_tier -> prod.create (kind media, owner the creator, delivery content of a members-only document or a new 'membership' delivery) + subs.create_plan(price, month); join -> subs.subscribe as the fan from its own account (status/period from sub_subs); cancel -> subs.cancel; the 'subscribers' content.access provider -> products.entitlement of the creator's product; then KNOWN_DUPLICATES creators.creator_members can go and tests/v5/test_gate_SP_6_2.py measures 1 system of record.

CORE-POP (population): `employed` could include an active labour-market employment contract (contracts.contracts employee = p<i>, status active) so the exogenous column becomes the cache D-21 asks for; economy.jobs treats individuals with an exogenous employer as not looking.

CIV (J): no recipe change needed - xchg founds two venues at genesis in population worlds (config venues='auto'), rivals runs display campaigns (display_ads), economy.work registers `jobs` and `assoc` where labor/inst are present (+2 habit slots: civ H=32 is enough, internet H=24 has room for ~22). Employment gets cross-subsystem edges once the first hire happens (labor.hired -> contracts, labor.shift -> support tickets), usually after day 3-6 of a civilisation.
